summary.headline: HLE Glascoat FY26 consolidated revenue rose 31.7% to INR1,353 crore, but EBITDA grew only 5.4% to INR148.5 crore as Omeras losses weighed.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR391.7 crore (up 17.4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR43.9 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT of INR20.1 crore (5.1% margin). FY26 EBITDA margin was 11% against a previously guided 16%, with management attributing the gap to the Omeras (Germany) EBITDA loss of INR15.3 crore, a INR2.1 crore labour-code charge and INR4.6 crore of acquisition costs. Management says the ongoing business runs at about 13.5% adjusted EBITDA margin and expects margins to keep rising in FY27. The Board recommended a 55% dividend for FY26, and the order book stood at about INR681.6 crore on March 31, 2026.

segments.name: Filtration, drying and other equipment
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR122 crore vs INR109 crore in Q4 FY25 (+11.9%); FY26 revenue up 50.9%.

segments.name: Glass lined equipment (GLE)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR219.5 crore vs INR167.9 crore (+29.2%); FY26 up 15.2%. Management puts adjusted GLE EBIT margin near 10% for FY26 and 11.5-12% in Q4, excluding Omeras.

segments.name: Heat transfer equipment (Kinam)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 7.4% YoY; FY26 revenue up 64.6%, with utilisation at about 70-75%. Analyst put FY26 revenue near INR200 crore.

segments.name: Omeras (Germany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue about INR43-44 crore; FY26 EBITDA loss INR15.3 crore and PAT loss INR15.6 crore. Management says it is close to EBITDA breakeven, which it estimates at about INR200-225 crore annual revenue. Order book about INR78-79 crore.

segments.name: Thaletec (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about EUR34 million (roughly INR345-350 crore at average FX). Low double-digit EBITDA margin (about 11-11.5% at EBIT level); top line stagnant after a softer Q3.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the ongoing business to reach about 16% EBITDA margin in the next two years, excluding Omeras; consolidated margin guided at 14-15%, with Germany dragging the average.
Omeras expected to reach double-digit standalone EBITDA margin in FY27 and to exceed INR200 crore annual revenue in FY26-27.
Heat transfer equipment expected to grow 15-20% per year for the next couple of years.
Consolidated revenue ambition of about INR2,000 crore in roughly two years, including Omeras; management said below that would be disappointing.
Indian Omeras tank-manufacturing capex expected to be commercially operational by end of FY27; revenue contribution to show in next year's financials.
capex_capacity: India GLE capacity utilisation now about 75%, up from the 60-65% previously cited; order inflow and pipeline described as improving.
Heat transfer (Kinam) utilisation about 70-75%; capacity creation planned from next year depending on how FY27 goes.
New Indian Omeras plant for tanks (biogas digesters, wastewater, ultra-pure water) expected commercially operational by end FY27; architectural products deferred in India for about 3 years.
Thaletec products now about 20% of Glass Lined India products in FY26.
demand_pricing: Pharma and API capex is the main demand driver in India; agrochemical and some specialty chemical customers deferred decisions after February 2026 because of the Iran-related geopolitical situation.
Gas prices for glass furnaces rose on the Iran conflict; management said most of the increase has been passed on to customers, with some impact.
Glass lined India value per equipment has fallen even as dispatch volumes rose 30-40%, so revenue has lagged output.
Exports from India were about 5-7% of India business revenue in FY26.
Expansion focus: Europe beyond Germany/Austria/Switzerland, US for Thaletec and Omeras, and Middle East for heat exchangers.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 16% FY26 EBITDA margin guidance from the Q2 call missed, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 guidance referred to H2 and FY27. Adjusted for Omeras, the ongoing business runs at about 13.5% EBITDA margin, and 16% is expected excluding Omeras in the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is Omeras on track to breakeven and double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Omeras is close to breakeven. Its order book roughly doubled from Dec-25 to Mar-26. Management expects double-digit margins on a standalone basis in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY26 revenue of about INR1,250 crore (ex-Omeras) reach INR2,000 crore in two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said below INR2,000 crore including Omeras would be disappointing. Consolidated margin is expected at 14-15%, with India above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Thaletec revenue for FY26?
Why has glass lined revenue been flat for several years?
qa_highlights.answer: Harsh Patel said equipment dispatch rose 30-40% but value per equipment fell sharply, so revenue has not grown in line with output.

risks_watch: Omeras turnaround: breakeven needs about INR200-225 crore annual revenue; quarterly EBITDA breakeven about INR45-50 crore.
Geopolitical deferrals in CDMO and agrochemical demand, and higher gas costs for glass furnaces.
Thaletec Germany top line flat in FY26; management expects a turnaround based on its order book.
Heat transfer growth is set at 15-20%, and new petrochemical and oil and gas entry means no established track record.
Consolidated margin gap versus earlier 16% guidance; FY27 margin recovery needs to show in Q1-Q2.
Integration load across four acquisitions while management builds the Omeras team.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and margin recovery, especially Omeras, India GLE and Thaletec. Cautious on near-term demand because of the Iran-related geopolitical situation, and evasive on how the FY26 margin shortfall compared with earlier guidance.
key_quotes: We remain confident about the long-term potential of the business and the meaningful contribution it will create from FY27 onwards.
If we do less than INR2,000 crores, we will be disappointed.
Omeras is now very close to breakeven, which is exactly what we had expected and what we had communicated at that point in time.

adds.what: New Indian Omeras plant for tanks (biogas digesters, wastewater, ultra-pure water)
Heat transfer (Kinam) capacity creation planned from next year, depending on FY27 performance

growth.why: Management guides to a ~INR2,000 crore consolidated revenue ambition in about two years including Omeras (implying roughly 48% growth from FY26's INR1,353 crore), 14-15% consolidated EBITDA margin and 15-20% heat transfer growth, backed partly by GLE utilisation at ~75%, an Omeras order book of ~INR78 crore and the Indian Omeras tank plant due by end FY27, but with no firm capacity or order number
